title: Evaluating an AI Medical Interpreter: Hospital Buyer's Guide
summary: A practical hospital guide to choosing an AI medical interpreter, including clinical evidence, safety, language coverage, workflow fit.
body_markdown:
###


Focus on product-specific clinical evidence, live safety controls, AI language coverage, workflow fit, pilot performance, security, and commercial fit.


###


Use realistic clinical scenarios with medications, numbers, negation, accents, interruptions, long patient answers, and background noise. Test how the system handles uncertainty and correction.


###


Ask for the full validation report, tested product version, languages, translation directions, comparator, reviewer method, error definitions, raw results, clinical severity, and study limitations.


###


Measure time to first interpreted sentence, successful session rate, clarification or repeat rate, meaning-sensitive quality findings, staff adoption, and cost per usable encounter.


###


The right number depends on your patient population. More important than the headline count is whether your highest-volume languages are truly AI-supported and have credible performance data.
